newsitem.title: USA: Ontario Hydro seeks U.S. power marketer license.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro seeks U.S. power marketer license.

text.p: Canada's Ontario Hydro said Thursday its U.S. subsidiary applied with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for a wholesale power marketer license.
The license would allow Ontario Hydro Interconnected Markets (OHIM Inc) to market power throughout the U.S.
Currently, it only sells electricity at the U.S. border.

"This license application is an example of how we are aggressively pursuing market opportunities as a result of deregulation in the U.S. electricity industry," David Goulding, president of OHIM, said in a statement.
Ontario Hydro said its sales from power export totaled C$233 million in 1995, and are projected to reach the C$250-300 million a year over the next few years.
Goulding said Ontario Hydro's initiatives to increase business in the U.S. reflect its anticipation of competition in the province's own electricity market.
